note: Seeds for the daily one-off reel (the owner, 2026-11-16: 'one off reels that follow a completely different format, but only for one reel... look at ALL reels in my niche'). Shapes, never words. Evidence: swipe.md (3,400 Shorts and TikToks ranked against their own accounts, 4 Nov to 15 Nov 2026), the Volume money tracker (623 posts from 334 accounts, measured 15 Nov 2026: each format worked for 3 or more accounts; x = multiple of the account's own median views), and the wide pull of 16 Nov. 'untested' = an idea of ours with no outside evidence. The writer may take one or invent its own.

ideas.shape: An empty numbered list, table or tier chart is on screen from frame 0 and each row fills in as the voice says it, no intro.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 9 accounts, median 16x (best 69x)

ideas.shape: An on-screen scoreboard fills in as the story goes (points for good habits, against for bad), the final score is the verdict.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 6 accounts, median 27x

ideas.shape: Name a famous money saying everyone repeats ('buy the dip', 'cut losses short'), break it on screen, then prove when it holds and when it lies.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 9 accounts, median 9x; the study of 2026-11-17: 'Stop using RSI on its default settings' 28x on a 998-view channel; 'Don't buy it, but put an order in' 47x (13M)

ideas.shape: A clueless character asks the obvious question ('Wait, isn't X supposed to...?'), an expert answers, the answer flips it inside 3.5 s.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 3 accounts, median 53x; swipe.md Sticky Academy 100x; the study of 2026-11-17: the same two-figure dialogue at 100x (170k on a 1,700 median) and 9.4x, one caps word on screen per beat, a real photo cutout of the famous head

ideas.shape: Two people start with the same 100,000 MB, make different choices at each step, and the final totals are compared side by side.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 7 accounts, median 6x; the study of 2026-11-17 (TikTok): the same person twice under two column labels with a fixed headline, tags stacking under each as said, two totals at the end: 18.9x (151k on 8,000) and 20.7x

ideas.shape: One exact amount itemised line by line: every MB of one trade accounted for (fee, spread, slippage, the loss, what was left).
ideas.evidence: Volume, 'budget one exact salary line by line': 8 accounts, median 12x

ideas.shape: A countdown from 5 to 1 that saves the best for last, each entry acted out in two seconds.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 5 accounts, median 11x

ideas.shape: A five-second wall of text too dense to read once, made to be paused and replayed; the voice gives only the hook.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 4 accounts, median 16x; swipe.md 15-truths loop 261x; the study of 2026-11-17: a silent 5-second card of nine candle patterns with BUY/SELL badges, 11x (200k views); a 'three inside up' pattern drawn in three frames, 9.5x

ideas.shape: Open on the finished result (the account at the end, the winning or ruined trade), then rewind to how it got there.
ideas.evidence: Volume 'start on the finished spread': 6 accounts, 7x; swipe.md result-first 20x

ideas.shape: A script for a scary moment, word for word: what to say to yourself (or a friend) when the margin call comes, the hot tip lands, the stock halves.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 4 accounts, median 45x

ideas.shape: The trades a calm trader said no to this week, each one shown and refused with its reason.
ideas.evidence: Volume 'show what you refused to buy': 4 accounts, 13x; 'things I don't buy' 14x

ideas.shape: The hook names one exact kind of viewer ('If you check your trades on the bus...'), and every line is for them.
ideas.evidence: Volume: 10 accounts, median 7x (best 170x)

ideas.shape: Every one of a kind explained at speed, one acted scene each (every order type, every way a trader blows up).
ideas.evidence: swipe.md stick figures: 'every financial scam explained' 67x, money-laundering 80x

ideas.shape: A present-tense paradox under a headline that stays on screen ('The company made record profits. The shares fell.'), one picture swapped per sentence.
ideas.evidence: swipe.md Casual Finance 14x, 10x

ideas.shape: 'This is what we call X' over one giant labelled object; a new label lands every two seconds.
ideas.evidence: swipe.md Rayner Teo 44x

ideas.shape: A made-up Meme Street company everyone knows in the game, the size of its fall, 'here's why', three numbered reasons.
ideas.evidence: swipe.md Unger Academy 47x; the study of 2026-11-17: '$700 BILLION' over a money bag, '-50%' over a red chart, three numbered reasons, 47x on a 422-view channel (a real company there; ours are fictional)

ideas.shape: A nature-documentary narrator observes traders in the wild, whispering: the herd buying the top, the lone patient one at the waterhole.
ideas.evidence: untested

ideas.shape: The whole reel is one group chat scrolling: the hype, the hot tip, the silence, the one friend with a plan.
ideas.evidence: untested (text stories: the faceless-channel guides of 2026 call them mainstream)

ideas.shape: A bad habit on trial: the prosecution shows the evidence, the habit's lame defence, the jury (the viewer) votes, the verdict.
ideas.evidence: untested

ideas.shape: A recipe for disaster, read like a cooking show: the ingredients of a blown account, mixed step by step, served.
ideas.evidence: untested

ideas.shape: A dating show: three made-up Meme Street companies introduce themselves to the viewer, red and green flags flash, the viewer picks one.
ideas.evidence: untested

ideas.shape: A market weather forecast for one made-up company: the news front coming in, the storm warning, what to carry.
ideas.evidence: untested

ideas.shape: A game show: the host, two contestants, buzzers, one money question with a surprising answer and a score at the end.
ideas.evidence: the 16 Nov pull: a broker's game-show reel 192x (an advert, so weak)

ideas.shape: A heist film in reverse: the crew plans to steal the viewer's money (fees, FOMO, leverage), the viewer's one rule foils them.
ideas.evidence: untested

ideas.shape: A till receipt prints line by line for one trade or one week of trading; the total at the bottom is the punchline.
ideas.evidence: untested; close to Volume's 'checkout total proof' (12 accounts, 6x)

ideas.shape: Two commentators call a trader's day like a match, with replays and a pundit's verdict at full time.
ideas.evidence: untested (our Instant replay format calls a chart; this calls a person)

ideas.shape: A question to the viewer on screen ('Would you quit if this happened to you?'), then a face reacting (a stick trader celebrating, then head in hands) over the chart as the trade hits the stop by a hair and runs to target; the viewer answers in the comments.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: 7.4x and 139 comments on 31k views, 17 seconds

ideas.shape: One tool everyone uses on its default; the exact numbers to type instead, one per kind of trader (5, 9, 14), each shown being typed into the settings box; the result on one chart.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: 28x on a 998-view channel; '84% win rate' with the indicator names 14x (410k)

ideas.shape: A premise that frames the whole reel: 'If I only had 60 seconds to reach every losing trader, this is what I'd say', a visible clock running down, the words landing one at a time, the last word on zero.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: 66x (280k on a 4,200 median)

ideas.shape: Before, the struggle card, after: three acts with a date on each ('Before trading (2023)', 'Then: 3 years', 'Now (2026)'), the same character in each, the middle act the longest; ours shows a habit changing, never money made.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: silent montages at 7.2x (3.5M, 1,000 comments) and 4x (486k, 562 comments); the shape, not the Lamborghini

ideas.shape: 'The exact setup I look for every morning': one scene per rule, each label landing on the chart as it is said (the band, acceptance, the first sign, entry, target hit), the trade box filling at the end; a one-word comment keyword.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: 10x and 622 comments on a 3,100-view channel

ideas.shape: Countries, companies or the market itself drawn as characters with eyes that talk to each other ('Don't worry, I'll buy it!'), a headline fixed at the top for the whole reel, a present-tense paradox.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: Casual Finance 14x (390k) and 10x (282k)

ideas.shape: A straight-faced parody of the niche's own clichés (the finance-bro podcast, the guru with the Lamborghini), fast, with one absurd number per line; the lesson is what they get wrong.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17: 12.7x (184k) with 496 comments

ideas.shape: A sum made physical: the thing held up on frame 0 (a box, a bill, a coin), each number typed on a calculator and held to camera, the price shown where it is paid, the total back on the calculator at the end; four places in thirty seconds.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17 (TikTok): 'Buying GTA 6 can save you $5,000', 10.3M at 8.2x with 5,212 comments

ideas.shape: Two characters with their money floating above their heads; a 'three years later' card; the numbers change while the characters stay; the ledger of both paths at the end.
ideas.evidence: the study of 2026-11-17 (TikTok): the loyalty-pays-less skit, 1.9M at 5.7x
